issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int plus a String reason), but the solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This parameter mismatch means code/tests expecting the two-parameter signature will not compile against the solution and will confuse students about the required method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem/UML by changing the solution method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update its body to add the new guest students (and optionally store or log the reason). Alternatively, if the intention was a single-parameter method, update the problem statement and UML to declare addGuestStudents(int) to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method addGuestStudents(int, String) that accepts a number of new guest students and a reason (int and String). In the solution implementation the method addGuestStudents is declared with only a single int parameter (no String reason). This mismatch in the method signature (same method name but different parameters) breaks the one-to-one mapping students expect between the task description and the reference implementation and will cause confusion when implementing or testing the required method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either update the solution and template to implement addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and use or document the reason parameter, or change the problem statement to require only addGuestStudents(int). Preferred fix: modify the solution and template to declare public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) { /* update numberOfGuestStudents and handle reason (e.g., log) */ } so it matches the problem specification.
